title: Bologna Sandwich on Wheat with Cheese

content.title: About
content.content: The Bologna sandwich on wheat with cheese is a classic handheld meal featuring thin slices of boiled Bologna sausage (or a similar cooked ham) placed between two slices of whole‑grain wheat bread and topped with a slice of meltable or firm cheese. It is popular as a quick snack and is often served in school cafeterias and casual cafés.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “Bologna” comes from the Italian city of Bologna, although the Russian version is usually a simple boiled ham without heavy seasoning.
Whole‑grain wheat bread provides slower‑digesting carbohydrates, making the sandwich more satiating than one made with white bread.
The combination of cheese and Bologna sausage supplies a complete set of essential amino acids.
During the Soviet era a similar sandwich was called “ham and cheese sandwich”; today the “Bologna” branding emphasizes a more premium image.
The sandwich packs well in plastic wrap, which is why it is a staple in school lunchboxes.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The sausage and cheese together provide about 15‑20 g of protein per serving, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Cheese contributes calcium needed for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Both the ham and cheese are sources of B1, B2, B6, and B12, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Whole‑grain wheat bread supplies fiber and slowly absorbed carbs, helping to keep blood‑sugar levels stable.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: The sausage provides heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Both the ham and cheese can be salty; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese and processed sausage contain saturated fats, and excessive intake may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk‑protein allergy.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Some Bologna sausages contain nitrites and other preservatives, which should be limited in the diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich can be eaten cold or lightly toasted. It is convenient to cut into bite‑size pieces for children or serve whole as a quick lunch. Add lettuce, tomato, or mustard for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the assembled sandwich refrigerated at 0‑4 °C and consume within 24 hours. If ingredients are stored separately, keep the sausage and cheese in airtight containers for up to 5 days, and store the bread in a dry place away from moisture.
